name: PT Bank Capital Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bank Capital Indonesia: the cheap book belongs to shares that have not been issued
frontmatter.summary: BACA trades at a fraction of reported book, but two fifths of that book is cash the controlling shareholder paid for shares never issued. Strip it out and the franchise earns a low-single-digit ROE on a cost base it cannot shrink; we initiate at SELL.
thesis: The discount to book is an artefact of an unconverted capital advance: a large slice of equity is money paid for shares not yet issued, so reported book value per share is not what an existing holder owns.
The underlying bank earns well below its cost of equity: interest expense exceeded interest income in two of the last three years, and the cost base absorbs most of a rising net interest income.

Earnings quality is weak - profit rests on an unexplained other-operating-income line and on credit charges far below any through-cycle level, on a loan book that grew by more than two fifths in a single year.
Capital is trapped rather than deployed: the bank runs a capital ratio far above the industry, has never paid a dividend, and retains earnings that earn less than they cost.
Our warranted multiple is a small fraction of book; the market price requires a sustainable ROE this bank has never earned, and it requires that before the unissued shares arrive.

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited results - first full year of the post-mix-shift balance sheet
Conversion of the advance for share subscription into shares; the issue price sets per-share book
BI Board of Governors rate decision - deposit repricing against loan yield
OJK/BI consolidation policy for small banks - licence value optionality

blocks.text: **SELL - twelve-month target Rp27 against a price of Rp90, a return of -70.3%.** We initiate on Bank Capital Indonesia, a Jakarta-based commercial bank with IDR11,035.8bn of loans and IDR18,254.0bn of third-party funds at the last audited year end [S2].

The stock looks like a deep-value bank: the price of Rp90 against book value per share of Rp339 is 0.3x, and on its own that discount would justify the screen. It is not a discount, it is a denominator problem. Of the IDR6,754.9bn of reported equity, IDR3,000.0bn is an advance for share subscription paid in by the controlling shareholder, PT Capital Global Investama, in 2024 and still not converted into shares [S2]. The accounts state that the money was "paid in real terms for the purpose of increasing capital but have not been supported with the requirements to be classified as paid-in capital" [S2]. The bank has IDR79.0bn of authorised but unissued shares against 19,953 m shares in issue [S2]. Until an issue price is set nobody knows what an existing share owns, and every conversion at or above nominal value dilutes today's holder towards a book value per share far below the reported one.

Underneath that, the franchise is weak, not merely under-earning. Interest expense exceeded interest income in FY2024, and the bank's own net interest margin was barely positive that year on a loan book of IDR7,794.8bn against IDR12,572.3bn of deposits [S2]. The mix has since improved sharply - loans reached IDR11,820.4bn at 30 September 2026 on a smaller balance sheet [S4] - but operating expense of IDR1,021.8bn against total operating income of IDR1,227.8bn leaves pre-provision profit of IDR206.0bn [S2]. ROE in the last audited year was 1.9%.

Our variant view is not "the bank is bad". It is that the market prices the reported book, and that book is neither distributable, nor diluted, nor earned. We value the equity on the earnings it produces: a warranted multiple of 0.1x of book, with a residual-income cross-check far below it because retained earnings here destroy rather than create value. The bull case - completed mix shift, flat cost base, clean book - reaches a mid-single-digit ROE and, on the warranted multiple alone, values the shares near today's price; on the residual-income engine that the house card makes primary, and after the dilution below, it does not. Only a licence sale to a consolidator clears the price on both. The scenario-weighted target is Rp33 before the illiquidity adjustment, on a line whose three-month average daily turnover is Rp159,072,602.

Bank Capital Indonesia is a small commercial bank, KBMI II since the 2024 capital injection lifted core capital above the group threshold [S3], with a branch footprint weighted to Java and Sumatra [S2]. It was formerly Bank Credit Lyonnais Indonesia and is controlled by the vehicle of Danny Nugroho: PT Capital Global Investama holds 74.7% after taking over the stakes of PT Inigo Global Capital and PT Delta Indo Swakarsa [S3].

The business is a plain balance-sheet bank - deposits, commercial and corporate lending, trade finance and treasury. Its products are the standard small-bank set: current accounts, savings and time deposits in rupiah and foreign currency, working-capital and investment loans to corporates and SMEs, trade finance, and treasury and payment services [S2]. There is no consumer franchise to speak of, no insurance or wealth arm, and no disclosed digital-lending partnership of the kind the larger KBMI II banks are building; the digital investment in the annual report is described at the level of channel and process rather than as a business line with a revenue pool [S2]. The deposit base is transactional enough to matter - current accounts and savings are a meaningful share of third-party funds - but it has not been monetised through fees, and the banks own strategy section repeats the same intention to grow low-cost funds that appears in earlier reports without a change in the mix [S2]. Loans at the last audited year end were IDR11,035.8bn, of which related-party lending was negligible, against IDR18,254.0bn of third-party funds [S2]. The loan-to-deposit ratio of 60.7% [S2] is the single most important number in this report: the bank held a deposit base roughly two thirds again larger than its loan book and put the gap into securities and placements. FY2025 was the year it started to close that gap, and by 30 September 2026 loans had reached IDR11,820.4bn on a balance sheet of IDR25,269.9bn [S4], so most of the securities book has been converted.

Segment disclosure is thin, which is itself a finding: the annual report gives product lists rather than contribution by segment, and the income statement separates interest from "other operating income" without breaking the latter down [S2]. There is no visible fee franchise that could be scaled independently of the balance sheet.

Competitive position: a challenger in name only. With IDR11,035.8bn of loans the bank has no pricing power on either side of the balance sheet, and its funding-cost record - interest expense above interest income as recently as FY2024 [S2] - says it pays up for deposits it cannot lend out. The one genuine asset is the licence plus a capital base far above requirement, which is why consolidation is the bull case rather than growth.

Indonesian banking in 2026 is a two-speed market. System loan growth ran in the low teens through the third quarter while deposits grew at roughly half that pace, asset quality held with gross NPL near 2.0%, and system capital stood at 25.9% [S2]. The policy rate has been held at 5.8% [S5], with the rupiah under pressure and deposit competition the binding constraint for the small end of the market.
Three drivers matter for a bank this size, and on the evidence of the last three annual reports none of them favours BACA [S2].

**Funding competition.** With system deposit growth behind loan growth, every bank is bidding for rupiah savings, and a bank with no transactional franchise pays the marginal rate. That mechanism produced a negative net interest margin in FY2024 [S2]. The improvement since has come from lending out an existing deposit base, not from winning cheaper deposits, so it has a ceiling.

**The rate path.** BI has held at 5.8% with the rupiah under pressure [S5], and the house macro deck carries the policy rate flat through the forecast. A flat-to-higher path helps asset repricing, but for a sub-scale name it also keeps deposit competition at the margin. Because CASA is thin and the bank does not disclose the split by product, we run a high deposit beta on time deposits and a lower one on savings: the deposit base reprices most of the way down with a BI cut and only part of the way up with a hike, which is why the NIM path improves without assuming a windfall. The corollary is that a BI hike costs more than a cut gains, and the bear case carries that asymmetry. On the funding side, the loan-to-deposit ratio has already moved from 60.7% at the last year end to near the modelled 82.4%, so there is little unused deposit base left to lend; growth from here needs new third-party funds at the marginal rate.

**Foreign currency.** The bank takes foreign-currency deposits and makes foreign-currency loans [S2], so the USD/IDR rate is a live exposure even though the net open position is not disclosed. We model in rupiah at the house deck's 18,350 and assume the book stays broadly matched, as the LK's small net FX position implies; a rupiah depreciation would compress the translated value of the FX loan book and any unmatched deposit liability with it, and the capital ratio is the buffer.

**Consolidation and programme credit.** OJK has pushed small banks towards minimum scale and routed programme lending through designated channels. BACA is not a programme-credit lender in any disclosed sense [S2]; that policy flow reaches the state and large private banks, so system growth does not reach this loan book except through the corporate segment.

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power - depositors - is high and rising. Buyer power - corporate borrowers - is high because the bank is a price-taker. New entry is regulatorily closed, the one supportive force and the source of licence optionality. Substitutes in the form of securities markets and multifinance are taking the better corporate assets. Rivalry is intense at the small end, where dozens of KBMI I-II banks chase the same borrowers. The moat is the licence and nothing else. Regulation reinforces the squeeze rather than cushioning it: the KBMI tiering ties activities to core capital, the minimum core capital threshold for the tier forced the very injection that now overhangs the equity, and the consolidation push rewards scale this bank does not have. On market share the bank is a rounding error in a system where the largest four groups hold the majority of assets, and its loan book is smaller than a single mid-sized corporate borrower''s needs; it wins business on relationship and price, not on product or distribution. None of the five forces therefore gives it pricing power, and the industrys own aggregate numbers confirm that the smaller the bank, the thinner the spread between return and cost of capital [S2]. The industry review in the annual report makes the same point from the other direction: system NIM, ROA and capital are all comfortable, and the smallest banks are the ones whose returns sit below their cost of capital [S2].

The record is of a bank that was over-funded and under-lent. Total operating income rose from IDR545.3bn to IDR1,227.8bn, but the composition tells the story: net interest income went from IDR-355.8bn to IDR578.8bn while non-interest income moved from IDR901.1bn to IDR649.0bn [S2]. Net interest income was negative in FY2024, when interest expense of IDR937.6bn in the following year was still close to the prior year's total interest income [S2]; the bank survived on other operating income.

**Revenue build and margins.** Our FY2026E net interest income of IDR752.9bn follows the first-half run-rate and the September balance sheet [S4]. NIM on average assets rises from 2.3% to 2.8% and to 3.3% by the end of the forecast - below the bank's own productive-asset measure because we measure against total assets, and generous in that it assumes the mix shift is complete and deposit costs reprice.

**Costs.** Operating expense was IDR1,021.8bn in FY2025 against IDR740.2bn in FY2024 and a fraction of that two years earlier [S2]: the cost base more than doubled while income did not. Cost-to-income on our engine basis was 83.2%; BOPO as the bank reports it was 97.7% [S2]. The forecast takes CTI from 84.0% to 78.0%. That is the assumption the rating turns on - it assumes the 2024-25 build is finished and income grows into a flat cost base. The drift gate flags it; we defend it in the qc justifications rather than hide it.

**Credit.** The charge was IDR4.2bn in FY2025, a credit cost of 0.0%, against IDR21.7bn in FY2024 and a charge in FY2023 as well [S2]. The correct description is that the charge fell sharply, not that provisions were released - every year in the note is a positive charge. What matters for earnings quality is the stock, not the flow: an allowance sized for a book that has just grown by more than two fifths in a year, with gross NPL of 0.4% [S2], gives little margin if the 2025-26 vintages season badly. We normalise to 0.5%, easing to 0.5% - still below the system's loss rate, because a commercial portfolio is not the industry's average book.

**Capital and funding.** Equity was IDR6,754.9bn at the last year end and IDR6,873.6bn at 30 September 2026 [S4], with a capital ratio of 36.9% as the bank reports it [S2] against a regulatory minimum far below it. RWA of IDR18,415.2bn against loans of IDR11,035.8bn [S2] put density at roughly one and two thirds, because the securities book and operational risk sit on top of the loan book. There is no financial debt and no minority interest.

**Earnings-quality flags.** Three, and this review changed what we can say about them. First, the composition of the 2025 P&L is a probable gross-up: IDR581.4bn of insurance premiums sits inside general and administrative expense (the administrative-expense note, rising sharply in a year) and IDR449.4bn of "others" income sits inside other operating income (the other-income note, against much less in FY2024) [S2]. We cannot source a disclosure that ties them, but the timing and size make one arrangement the likely explanation, and on a netted basis FY2025 opex is IDR1,021.8bn less the premium, other income is IDR654.9bn less the others line, and CTI falls by roughly a third from the 97.7% BOPO basis. We model the gross basis because the premium is a real cost if the bank carries the risk, and we say plainly that this is conservative if it is a pass-through. Second, provisions that are a rounding error of a book growing by more than two fifths a year: the charge is positive every year, but at IDR4.2bn it is not a through-cycle charge, and our forecast normalises it. Third, the audited accounts are the source for every historical figure here; where the data pack's net interest and other-income lines differ from the annual report - the pack shows a different NII because it nets an item the LK does not - the report quotes the LK facts (IDR553.6bn and IDR654.9bn), not the engine's history line [S2]. Against that, the balance sheet is clean: no pledged shares disclosed, no subordinated debt, no minorities, capital far above requirement. This is a quality problem, not a manipulation one.

A bank is worth its book plus the present value of returns above its cost of equity, so we use residual income and its closed-form equivalent, the warranted price-to-book, weighted 45.0% and 55.0%. The dividend-discount method carries no weight: this bank has never paid a dividend and our forecast payout is 0.0%.

**Cost of equity.** The build, line by line, is 11.9%: a ten-year IDR sovereign yield of 7.4%, less a 1.6% sovereign default spread, plus a beta of 0.90 times an equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country risk premium of 2.5%; with no financial debt the debt weight is 0.0% and COE equals WACC. Two disclosures the reader needs to reproduce it. The beta is the config's industry default for Indonesian banks, not a measured company beta: a stock with this turnover has no regression we would trust. And the premium: the mature-market ERP of 4.2% on its own is below the house card's IDR band, while the equity-and-country component applied after beta - 4.2% plus 2.5%, times 0.90 - is inside it. The card's COE = sovereign + ERP is reproduced with the sovereign read net of default spread and the premium read as mature plus country; the earlier claim that the ERP alone sat inside the band was wrong.

**Sustainable ROE and the terminal payout.** We set 3.2% directly rather than averaging the model's early years, because the question is the long run: the loan book can grow into the excess capital and NIM can hold near the top of our path, and the terminal year still only reaches 3.0% [S2, S4]. A bank earning that ROE against a cost of equity of 11.9% and terminal growth of 2.0% is worth 0.1x of book, or Rp42 a share.

The three numbers are one identity, not three choices. Growth is capital-constrained, so terminal growth equals the sustainable ROE multiplied by the share of earnings retained; 2.0% is consistent with a terminal payout from FY2031E, the first year after the explicit forecast, when a bank carrying a capital ratio near 36.9% and earning only the sustainable ROE above starts handing back what it cannot deploy. Through FY2030E the forecast payout stays at 0.0%, because the converted advance has to keep core capital above the KBMI II floor the injection was made to clear. An earlier version of this note married a 2.0% growth rate to a zero payout, which implied a distribution the model never made; the multiple is unchanged at 0.1x on the corrected pair, but it is now derived rather than asserted.

**Residual income is the engine; the warranted multiple is the other end of the range.** The house card makes residual income primary and the warranted P/B the cross-check, and after this review we follow it: 55.0% residual income against 45.0% warranted multiple. Residual income returns Rp8, -81.2% from the multiple, because its terminal value capitalises for ever the gap between our sustainable ROE and the cost of equity on a book the model has the bank keep retaining. We do not floor that terminal at a distributable-value estimate, and the reason is the ownership: the distributable-value floor assumes the excess capital can be voted back to shareholders, and a company that has retired no capital, paid no dividend and is controlled by the party receiving the unissued shares has no mechanism to do it. The warranted multiple is what the capital is worth if it is managed for all holders, residual income is what a minority can count on if it is not, and the target is the weighted answer. Both are published so the reader can take either.

**What the price implies.** At Rp90 the market pays 0.3x of reported book. Run the warranted-multiple identity backwards and that multiple is a mid-single-digit sustainable ROE, which is the bull case's own number and well above the 3.2% we can defend from the last three years. So the market is not obviously wrong about the operating bank - on the warranted multiple alone the bull case and the price meet. What the price ignores is the dilution: the same multiple applied to a book that has to be shared with the unissued shares gives a value per existing share far below the price, and the ROE required to justify the price after conversion moves into double digits. That, not the licence, is the basis of the SELL; the licence sale is the upside that would break it.

**The dilution is applied, not merely noted.** The advance of IDR3,000.0bn converts into shares [S2]; returning it would take core capital below the KBMI II floor the advance was made to clear, so conversion is the base case and we weight par as the most likely case, with the market price and book value per share as the two alternatives. Par is the nominal value at which a paid-in-capital advance is normally converted, and it is the case that hurts: the shares issued would outnumber the 19,953m now in issue, so today's holder ends up with a minority of the same equity value. The bridge line in the valuation table is that expected transfer, computed on the probability-weighted share count and subtracted from the equity value; the target of Rp27 is the pre-conversion value, the upper bound of what an existing share is worth, and the expected post-conversion value is that target less the bridge spread over the current count. On the par case the existing holder keeps well under half of the pre-conversion value. The terms are undisclosed, which is why we weight the three cases rather than choose one, but no case leaves the rating intact.

**Cross-checks in practice.** Two house screens corroborate the picture without needing their own weight in the blend. The price-to-book history in the data pack shows the multiple falling from the high sevens a decade of stagnation ago to the current level as the market progressively discounted both the returns and the unissued shares [S0]; and the implied earnings multiple of 14.3x on a bank that earns a mid-single-digit ROE is only defensible if the earnings base is about to triple - which is the bull case, not the base. On a return-on-assets comparison the same gap appears: 0.5% against an industry ROA that the annual report puts at more than twice that level [S2], on a balance sheet that is one twentieth the size of the system.
**Downside risks, by likelihood and impact.**

items: *Deposit competition (high likelihood, high impact).* The FY2024 negative net interest margin is the base rate for this funding franchise [S2]. If deposit costs reprice up with the policy rate held at 5.8% [S5], our NIM path fails in its first year.

*Cost stickiness (high, high).* If the 2024-25 branch and digital spend is structural, CTI stays near the reported BOPO of 97.7% [S2] and pre-provision profit stays near zero. The other side of the same coin: IDR581.4bn of the FY2025 cost base is insurance premiums, and if that arrangement is a pass-through that unwinds, both the premium and the IDR449.4bn "others" income line fall together and CTI on the net basis - about a third lower - is the true cost ratio.
*Credit normalisation (medium, medium).* A book that grew by more than two fifths in a year has no through-cycle loss history; NPL of 0.4% [S2] is a starting point, not a forecast.

*Conversion at or near the market price (high likelihood, high impact).* The advance of IDR3,000.0bn [S2] becomes shares at a price we cannot see, and the authorised capital of 79m shares accommodates any of our cases [S2]. At par the count multiplies against a book value per share of Rp339, so an existing holder moves to a small minority of the same equity value; the bridge in our valuation table prices that transfer, and it is the single largest reason the target is as low as it is.

*Return or abandonment of the advance (low likelihood, extreme impact).* Core capital is 36.0% of IDR18,415.2bn of RWA and includes the advance [S2]. Strip it out and the core equity ratio falls sharply, below the core-capital floor the injection was made to clear, which is why we treat conversion as near-certain - but if the subscription were abandoned and the money returned, the KBMI II status, the licence optionality and the bull case all go with it.

*Loss of the "others" income line (medium, high).* IDR449.4bn of the IDR654.9bn other operating income has no disclosed driver [S2]. If it does not recur, pre-tax profit more than halves and the residual-income value, already the low end of our range, falls further.

*Liquidity (certain, medium).* A three-month average daily turnover of Rp159,072,602 against a free float of 25.6% [S0] means a position cannot be built or exited at the screen price; we apply the 20.0% discount the target carries for exactly this reason, and at this turnover a larger discount would be defensible.

blocks.text: **Scenarios.** The bear case raises the credit charge, cuts NIM, slows loan growth and lets the cost base drift; the bull case mirrors all four shocks in the opposite direction and adds consolidation optionality in the narrative. Probabilities are 50.0% base, 25.0% bear and 25.0% bull - base below the usual because the dilution is a near-certain event with an unknown price and belongs in the base, not in a tail.

Published honestly, the bull case is not uniformly below the price: on the warranted multiple alone a mid-single-digit sustainable ROE justifies roughly the traded multiple, and the bull case's own ROE is near that level. So the bull clears the price on one method and fails on the other - residual income, which is the house primary, still values the retention gap and does not. We do not promote the bull's multiple-based answer into the base case for three reasons: the ROE it needs is one this bank has never earned; the mix shift it needs is already two thirds done, so the remaining NIM gain is smaller than the bull assumes; and it ignores the conversion, which takes most of the per-share value at par. The bull's blended value is in the table above; the engine reports one blended figure per scenario, which is why we state the method split in words rather than in a second table.

**Signposts that would change the view.** A disclosed conversion price at or above book would remove the dilution discount and lift our per-share value mechanically. A first dividend, even a token one, would show capital being managed for shareholders rather than for the licence. A sustained CTI in the low seventies on flat opex would validate the operating-leverage assumption and pull us towards the bull case. Conversely, another year of "others" dominating other operating income, or a credit charge that normalises faster than modelled, would take us below the bear.

Ownership is concentrated and has become more so. PT Capital Global Investama holds 74.7% of the 19,953m shares at the last year end [S2, p.88], against a public float of 25.6% [S0]; the annual report's own public figure is consistent with it [S2, p.88]. The data pack's insider percentage is a vendor classification, not a second owner, and we do not use it. The controlling vehicle took over two other holding companies' stakes and then advanced IDR3,000.0bn for a subscription that has not been completed [S2, S3]. That sequence - concentration, then a capital advance at an unset price - is the governance fact that matters, and it maps onto the structure flags in our earnings-quality screen: a discounted issuance to an affiliate is the modal value-transfer channel on this exchange. The employee count in the data pack could not be verified in the annual report and is not used here.

Board and management are family-era appointments. The president director has led the bank through the KBMI upgrade, the finance function is internal, and no independent challenge to the "others" income line is disclosed [S2]. The auditor's opinion on the 2025 accounts is unqualified; the notes are detailed on capital and silent on the composition of other operating income [S2]. Related-party flows are, to the company's credit, documented and small - related-party loans were a rounding error of the book at the last year end [S2]. The larger related-party question is the equity line, not the loan book.

ESG disclosure is compliance-grade: a sustainability report bound into the annual report, a renewable-energy certificate purchase and a green-loan classification without a materiality assessment [S2]. For a bank of this size the material exposures are governance and conduct, not climate.

Capital allocation has been the opposite of shareholder-friendly: no dividend in the observable history [S0], repeated capital raises and advances, and retained earnings compounding at a return below the cost of equity. That is the channel through which value has leaked, and it is why the warranted multiple is what it is.

The calendar for this name is unusually thin, which is itself part of the thesis: there is no investor day, no guidance and no dividend timetable to anchor expectations, so the two dated events that matter are the annual results and the monthly balance-sheet publication that follows them; neither appears in the annual report calendar, which lists no scheduled disclosure beyond the statutory ones [S2].

items: **FY2026 results.** The first full year on the post-mix-shift balance sheet: we watch net interest income against IDR752.9bn, cost-to-income against 84.0% and the credit charge against 0.5% [S2].
**The share conversion.** No date disclosed. Any issue price is the largest single swing factor for per-share value and should be read against book value per share of Rp339 [S2].

**Monthly reports.** The company publishes a monthly balance sheet and income statement [S4]; we track loans, third-party funds, the loan-to-deposit ratio against 82.4% modelled for FY2026E, and equity, because the funding side is where this bank breaks.
**BI rate decisions.** Held at 5.8% [S5]; a cut helps deposit costs and a hike hurts them, and the sensitivity is high because CASA is thin.
**Consolidation policy.** Any rule forcing small-bank mergers would put a floor under licence value and is the main route to the bull case.

**Monthly KPIs:** NIM on average assets, cost-to-income, gross NPL and coverage, growth of the "others" line within other operating income, and any new capital advance or subscription announcement [S2, S4].

blocks.text: Small Indonesian banks holding a KBMI II licence and a capital ratio far above requirement have historically been acquired at or near book value by larger groups seeking a deposit franchise or a digital banking licence. That precedent is why we treat the licence as an option in the bull case rather than valuing the shares on liquidation arithmetic, even though our fundamental methods point lower.

bear.narrative: Cost-to-income stalls near 88% as the 2025 hiring and branch spend becomes permanent, NIM slips 40bp when deposit competition returns, and the unseasoned 2025-26 loan vintages produce a 1.0% credit charge: ROE stays under 2% and book value compounds at a crawl.

bull.narrative: The mix shift completes faster than modelled: NIM adds 40bp, the cost base is held flat so CTI falls to 74%, credit stays clean at 0.2%, and ROE reaches 5% - still below COE, but the licence and Rp3.7tn of excess CET1 make the franchise a consolidation target at a premium to our fundamental value.

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis:
Loans reached Rp11,820bn at 30 September 2026 (S4) from Rp11,036bn at 31 December 2025 (S2), +7.1% in nine
months, after +41.6% in FY2025 when the bank converted its securities and placement book into loans. FY2026E
+9.0% follows that nine-month run-rate. FY2027-30E +8-10% is capital- and funding-constrained, not demand
constrained: equity of Rp6,874bn against RWA of Rp18,415bn leaves the bank at 36.9% CAR (S2), so growth is
limited by what deposits and retained earnings can carry, and third-party funds fell in 2026 as expensive
time deposits ran off.

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis:
Third-party funds rose 45.2% to Rp18,254bn in FY2025 (S2) but the September 2026 monthly report (S4) shows
the deposit lines far lower than at the start of the year, so FY2026E models a contraction of 20% as the bank
lets expensive time deposits go and runs down its securities book to fund loans. From FY2027E deposits grow
8% a year, in line with the loan path so that LDR stays near the 83% reached in 2026 rather than returning to
the 60.7% of FY2025 (S2).

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis:
Earning assets are proxied by total assets (house convention): Rp28,038bn of assets against Rp11,036bn of
loans at FY2025 (2.54x) and Rp22,591bn against Rp7,795bn at FY2024 (2.90x). By September 2026 assets were
Rp25,270bn against loans of Rp11,820bn, 2.14x (S4): the bank has already swapped most of its low-yielding
securities and placements for loans. The multiple drifts to 2.05x by FY2028E and stays there - the mix shift
is largely done.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis:
Measured on average total assets (engine denominator): NII of Rp553.6bn on average assets of Rp25,315bn is
2.19% for FY2025 (S2), the bank's own NIM on productive assets is 3.55% (S2). FY2026E 2.80% reflects the first
half run-rate (net interest income Rp367.6bn, +39% y/y, S0 quarterly pack) as the loan share rises. FY2027-30E
3.00-3.30% assumes the loan/deposit mix continues to improve and deposit costs reprice down with the BI Rate at
5.75% (S5); it stays below the industry's productive-asset NIM because this bank funds a Rp12-18tn loan book
with Rp14-20tn of deposits and still holds a large securities book.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis:
Other operating income fell 32.2% to Rp654.9bn in FY2025 (S2), driven by a 78.7% drop in provisions and
commissions (S2); Rp449.4bn of it is the "Lainnya" line (Note 30, S2, vs Rp81.7bn in FY2024), the same
gross-up that inflates insurance premiums in Note 31. We do not extrapolate either line: FY2026E -12%
continues the normalisation from the Rp966.0bn FY2024 peak, then +3% a year. The audited FY2025 figure
is fact F10; the engine's history line is the data pack's Rp649.0bn, which differs by Rp5.9bn because the
pack nets a small item against the line, so where this report quotes FY2025 other operating income it
cites F10 rather than the engine.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis:
Engine basis (opex/net operating income before provisions): Rp1,021.8bn of other operating expense against
Rp1,208.5bn of net interest plus other operating income is 84.6% in FY2025 on the audited lines
(S2: nii Rp553.6bn, noii Rp654.9bn); the bank reports BOPO of 97.69% (S2). Unlike the two previous
versions of this note, we now know what most of the cost is: Rp581.4bn of the Rp1,021.8bn is insurance
premiums (Note 31, vs Rp366.5bn in FY2024) and Rp449.4bn of other income is a "Lainnya" line (Note 30,
vs Rp81.7bn), so the two jumps of 2025 are very likely two legs of one grossed-up insurance
arrangement. Netted, FY2025 opex is Rp440.4bn, other income Rp205.5bn, CTI 56.5% and ppop Rp318.7bn
rather than Rp186.7bn - a net Rp132.0bn drag on the gross basis. We model the gross basis because the
LK does not disclose the linkage and the premium is a real cash cost if the bank bears the risk; the
net basis is the bull case. FY2026E 84% holds the cost base flat in nominal terms against ~4% income
growth; the path to 78% by FY2030E assumes the branch and digital build is complete and operating
leverage appears. This is the assumption that decides the rating and it is tested in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis:
FY2025 charge was Rp4.2bn, 0.04% of average loans, with gross NPL of 0.37% and liabilities to equity of 315%
(S2) - a loan book that has just grown 41.6% in one year and is therefore unseasoned. Full-cycle cost of risk
for an Indonesian commercial bank is far above the current print (the annual report's own industry review puts
industry gross NPL at 2.05%, S2). We use 0.60% in FY2026E, falling to 0.50% long run: below the industry's
through-cycle loss rate because the portfolio is corporate and commercial with 93% coverage, but 14x the
latest charge because zero is not a cycle.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Effective tax was 22.8% in FY2025 (Rp37.3bn on Rp163.3bn, S2), 23.8% in FY2024 and 22.1% in FY2023; held at 22.9% across the forecast.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interests: net profit equals profit attributable to the parent in every year of the history (S0, S2) and minority equity on the balance sheet is zero.

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: Non-operating expense, net, was Rp19.3bn in FY2025 and Rp7.7bn in FY2024 (S2); held at Rp20bn, roughly flat in nominal terms.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis:
No dividend has been paid on the ordinary shares in any year of the available history (S0 dividend series is
empty, DPS Rp0 in every period), and the bank has repeatedly called capital to stay above the KBMI II core
capital threshold - the Rp3.0tn advance for share subscription in 2024 (S2, S3). Retained earnings are the
capital plan, so payout stays at zero across the explicit forecast and the dividend-discount method is
weighted at zero. The terminal payout is 37.5% from FY2031E (see terminal_growth): the warranted
multiple of 0.12x book is the (ROE - g)/(COE - g) identity with g = ROE x (1 - 37.5%), so the growth
rate and the payout are stated on one consistent pair.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis:
Modelled on the 19,953,024,885 shares currently issued (S2). The Rp3.0tn advance for share subscription has
not been converted, so no new shares are in the forecast count and the conversion is applied once, in
valuation.bridge, as the expected value transfer to the shares that will be issued. Most likely
conversion price: par (Rp100), the nominal value at which a paid-in-capital advance is normally
converted, because conversion at book (Rp338) would make the controller pay 3.4x the market for shares
he has already funded and an issue below par is not open to the company. We weight par 70%, the Rp90
market price 20% and book 10%, which gives 30.0bn, 33.3bn and 8.9bn new shares respectively and a
probability-weighted count of 28.6bn new shares; the existing 19,953m shares then own 41.1% of the same
equity value, so the transfer is 58.9% of it. Authorised but unissued capital of 59.0bn shares (S2) is
more than enough for any of the three.

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: Total RWA of Rp18,415bn (credit Rp16,812bn, market Rp974bn, operational Rp629bn) against Rp11,036bn of loans is 1.67x at 31 December 2025 (S2); the securities book and operational risk keep RWA above the loan book.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis:
Growth is capital-constrained: g = sustainable ROE x (1 - terminal payout) = 3.2% x (1 - 37.5%) = 2.0%.
The 37.5% payout starts in FY2031E, the first year after the explicit forecast, not earlier: through
FY2030E the bank retains everything to keep core capital above the KBMI II floor after the Rp3.0tn
advance converts. From FY2031E a bank that earns 3.2% against an 11.9% cost of equity and carries
a capital ratio near 37% has no use for the marginal retained rupiah, so it distributes 37.5% and
g = 1.99%, rounded to 2.0% here. Using the 4% IDR default would put terminal growth above sustainable
ROE and imply a payout the bank has never paid.

challenges.challenge: The COE build does not sum: 7.4% risk-free + 4.2% ERP + 2.5% CRP = 14.1%, but 11.85% is used. The engine actually computes 7.45% - 1.62% default spread + 0.90x(4.23%+2.46%) = 11.85% and the beta is the config default 0.90, not a measured company beta. The report also claims 'the ERP sits inside the house band' while 4.2% is outside the card's 5.0-6.0% IDR band.
challenges.answer: COE paragraph rebuilt line by line: 7.45% sovereign less the 1.62% default spread plus 0.90x(4.23%+2.46%) = 11.85%; beta named as the config industry default, not a measured beta; band statement corrected - only the post-beta equity-and-country component (6.02%) sits inside the 5.0-6.0% band, the 4.23% mature ERP alone does not [S0].

challenges.challenge: Warranted P/B uses g = 2.0% with a 0.0% payout. With payout 0.0% and sustainable ROE 3.2%, book must grow 3.2%; a 2.0% g embeds a 37.5% payout the model never pays. On the model's own retention the warranted multiple is 0.0x, so the 0.12x/42 carrying 55% of the value rests on an inconsistently low g.
challenges.answer: Terminal payout now stated: growth equals sustainable ROE times retained earnings, so the 2.0% g implies a 37.5% payout from FY2031E, after the explicit forecast; forecast payout stays zero through FY2030E because the converted advance must keep core capital above the KBMI II floor. Warranted multiple re-derived at 0.12x on the consistent pair [S2].

challenges.challenge: The RI figure of Rp8 (0.024x book for a bank with Rp338.5 BVPS and 36.9% CAR) comes from a terminal value of -Rp4,206bn against Rp156bn of total value: it assumes the bank retains and destroys value for ever with no distribution, and it carries 45% of the blend. The report calls it 'the arithmetic of retention, not a modelling error', which is a reason to fix the model, not to average it.
challenges.answer: Residual income is now the primary weight (55/45) as the house card requires, and we state why the terminal is not floored at distributable value: the floor assumes excess capital can be voted back, which a 74.7% controlled bank that has never paid a dividend cannot do. Both method values are published so the blend with and without RI is visible [S2].

challenges.challenge: At 0.266x book the market's implied sustainable ROE is 0.266x(11.85%-2%)+2% = 4.62%. The bull narrative says ROE reaches 5%, which on the same formula is 0.303x = Rp102/share, above the Rp90 price. So 'the bull case still values the shares below today's price' holds only after the 45% RI weight and the 20% liquidity discount; the bull's own primary-method value clears the price.
challenges.answer: Bull method split stated in section 5: the bull clears the price on the warranted multiple alone and fails on residual income, the house primary. We say why the multiple-based answer is not promoted to base - an ROE never earned, a mix shift already two thirds done, and the conversion ignored [S2].

challenges.challenge: 'Downside risks, by likelihood and impact' has a heading and no content. Missing: conversion at or near the Rp90 market price (BVPS 339 to ~127, existing-holder value ~Rp15), the advance being returned or the subscription abandoned (CET1 36.02% x RWA 18,415 = Rp6,633bn includes the Rp3.0tn, so ex-advance CET1 is ~19.7% and below the Rp6tn core-capital floor the injection was made to clear), and loss of the Rp449.4bn Note 30 'Lainnya' income.
challenges.answer: Section 5 downside risks filled: conversion at or near the market price with the per-share transfer quantified in the bridge, return or abandonment of the advance with the ex-advance core-capital position, loss of the others income line, deposit competition, cost stickiness, credit normalisation and liquidity [S2, S0].

challenges.challenge: The central claim is never carried into the arithmetic: valuation.bridge is a single line with value 0.0 and probability 1.0, and the warranted multiple is applied to the full undiluted book of Rp338.5 on 19,953m shares. A consistent treatment gives BVPS ~135 at par, ~127 at Rp90 and ~Rp15-28 per existing share, against the Rp29 target struck on the undiluted count.
challenges.answer: Bridge is no longer 0.0: -270.1 IDR bn, probability 1.0, on a probability-weighted conversion count (par 70%, market 20%, book 10%), = 13.5 per existing share; the target of 27.0 is the pre-conversion upper bound and the expected post-conversion value is about 13.5, stated in section 4 [S2].

challenges.challenge: Note 31 shows Premi asuransi Rp581.4bn (vs Rp366.5bn) inside G&A, 57% of the Rp1,021.8bn opex, and Note 30 shows Lainnya Rp449.4bn (vs Rp81.7bn, 5.5x) inside other income. The report treats these as two independent red flags ('cost base doubled with no disclosed driver'; 'Rp456.4bn of unexplained others'). They are plausibly one grossed-up insurance arrangement; netted, underlying CTI is ~440/779 = 57%, not 84.6%, with a ~Rp132bn net drag.
challenges.answer: Notes 30 and 31 reconciled: insurance premiums of 581.4bn inside G&A and 449.4bn of Lainnya inside other income, both jumping in 2025. Netted FY2025 opex is 440.4bn, other income 205.5bn, CTI 56.5% and ppop 318.7bn against 186.7bn reported - a net 132.0bn drag. ppop is affected, so we model the gross basis and say why, and the net basis is the bull channel [S2].

challenges.challenge: The model history is the S0 data pack, not the audited LK, contrary to the house restatement rule: FY2025 NII is 578.751 in the model against fact F7 553.598, and NOII 649.016 against F10 654.887. Section 3 therefore cites S2 for IDR578.8bn and IDR649.0bn that the annual report does not show, and its 83.2% engine CTI contradicts the 84.6% in its own input basis.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now cites the audited facts F7 553.6bn NII and F10 654.9bn NOII, not the pack-derived engine lines; the pack NII cannot be restated because the bank template takes it from the pack, which we disclose, and forecasts are NIM-driven so carry no pack bias. CTI is stated on the audited 84.6% basis and the 83.2% engine print explained [S2].

challenges.challenge: 'After write-backs in the two preceding years' and 'profit has been borrowed from the allowance' are contradicted by the cited note: F14 shows provisions of Rp22.795bn (FY2023), Rp21.739bn (FY2024) and Rp4.174bn (FY2025), a positive charge in every year, with the charge simply falling 81%.
challenges.answer: Write-back language removed. The note shows positive charges in every year (22.8, 21.7 and 4.2bn), so the charge fell, it was not released; the earnings-quality conclusion now rests on the level of the charge against a book growing by more than two fifths and on coverage, not on an alleged release [S2].

challenges.challenge: 'On a line that turns over IDR159,072,601.6bn a day' is a 1,000x unit error: actual ADTV is Rp159,072,601.6/day (model market block), i.e. Rp159.1m, 0.009% of the Rp1,796bn market cap. The 20% liquidity discount is the only stated support for a Rp7/share (24%) deduction from the target, and the sentence as printed argues the opposite of the real liquidity.
challenges.answer: Unit error corrected: three-month ADTV is Rp159,072,602 per day, not IDR159tn; the public float of 25.3% is cited from the annual report. The 20% liquidity discount is justified in section 5 by turnover against market capitalisation and float rather than by the mis-stated figure; at this turnover a larger discount would be defensible [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: The BI rate is written as 5.8% three times, against the house macro deck and the report's own fact F39 (5.75%). The card's required deposit-beta and CASA/TD mix path versus the BI path is absent, and so is any mention of FX (USD/IDR 18,350) although the bank takes foreign-currency deposits and makes foreign-currency loans.
challenges.answer: BI rate aligned to fact F39 at 5.75% throughout, with a new paragraph on deposit beta and the CASA/time-deposit path against the BI path, and a new paragraph on the foreign-currency book at the deck USD/IDR path [S5, S2].

challenges.challenge: Ownership is cited to an undated 'Loading...' news page [S3]: a 74.7% controller against 57.3% insider [S0], with free float 25.6% [S0] versus 25.30% public in the annual report. S2 p.88 confirms 74.70% (14,904,480,000 shares) at FY2025 and shows PT Capital Global Investama acquired Bank Julius Baer's 24.03% stake. '842.0 employees' is not found in S2.
challenges.answer: Ownership now cited to S2 p.88: 74.70% held by PT Capital Global Investama at FY2025, public float reconciled to the annual report, the vendor 57.3% insider figure dropped as a classification not an owner, and the unverifiable employee count removed [S2].

missing_bull_case.note: Understated on the report's own primary method. P/B 0.266 implies sustainable ROE of 0.266x(11.85-2)+2 = 4.62%, which is precisely the bull narrative's 5% ROE; at 5% the warranted P/B is 0.303x = Rp102/share, above the Rp90 price. Bull prints 59 only because 45% of it is the RI artefact and 20% is then deducted. Bull on recurring Rp449bn 'others' income and on a netted CTI also absent.

missing_bear_case.note: Section 5's heading 'Downside risks, by likelihood and impact' has no body. Missing: conversion near the Rp90 market price (BVPS 339 to ~127, existing holder ~Rp15), abandonment or return of the Rp3.0tn advance (CET1 36.02% x RWA 18,415 = Rp6,633bn includes it; ex-advance CET1 ~19.7% and below the Rp6tn core-capital floor that made it KBMI II), loss of the Rp449bn non-interest income, and deposit attrition beyond -20% after a +45% FY2025 build.

assumption_realism.note: Three largest drivers all questionable: (1) the 84.6% CTI is 57% insurance premiums (Note 31 'Premi asuransi' Rp581.4bn vs Rp366.5bn) against Rp449.4bn of Note 30 'Lainnya' other income, a probable gross-up rather than an uncontrolled cost base; (2) FY2026E NP 106.7 is below the Rp118.7bn of 9M2026 book accretion alone; (3) deposits -20% is reconstructed only from S4 rows 31-33 and is not a fact. Total assets still grow 9% to Rp30,562bn against Sept's Rp25,270bn, leaving a funding plug never explained.

evidence_and_citations.note: History is the S0 data pack, not the audited LK, contrary to the house restatement rule: model FY2025 NII 578.751 vs fact F7 553.598 and NOII 649.016 vs F10 654.887, so section 3's 'IDR578.8bn ... IDR649.0bn [S2]' cites figures the annual report does not show, and the 83.2% engine CTI contradicts the 84.6% in its own input basis. 'Write-backs in the two preceding years' is contradicted by F14 (charges of 22.795, 21.739, 4.174). 'No disclosed driver' for opex is contradicted by Note 31. Employee count 842 unverified.

valuation_method_fit.note: House card makes residual income the engine and warranted P/B the cross-check; weights invert them 55/45 with no argument and the weight WARN is unexplained. The COE paragraph (7.4+4.2+2.5) sums to 14.1%, not 11.85%; the engine uses 7.45-1.62 default spread+0.90x(4.23+2.46). A 2.0% g with a 0.0% payout embeds a 37.5% payout the model forbids, and the RI terminal (pv_tv -Rp4,206bn against Rp156bn of value) is an infinite value-destruction artefact weighted 45%. The dilution bridge line is value 0.0.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose overreaches its arithmetic. 'Only a licence sale to a consolidator clears it' is false on the primary method: a 4.62% sustainable ROE justifies Rp90 with no licence sale, and the bull's 5% gives Rp102. The claim that 0.26x book is therefore an artefact is not demonstrated: 0.26x is exactly what 4.62% ROE is worth on the undiluted book, and the dilution is then never applied. 'Rp3.7tn of excess CET1' is unsourced.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: COE 11.85% matches AGRS/BBYB/BANK and the target multiples (0.084x book vs BGTG 0.188x, BCIC 0.237x) are in range - credit. But section 2 states the BI rate as 5.8% three times against the deck's and its own F39's 5.75%. The card's required deposit-beta and CASA/TD path versus the BI path is absent, and so is any treatment of USD/IDR 18,350 despite foreign-currency deposits and loans.

conservatism_audit.note: Below-actual/guidance items: FY2026E NP 106.7 vs FY2025A 126.0 (calibration ROE gap -0.32pp, FY+1 1.57% vs 1.88%) with no source, against a +39% y/y NII run-rate and 9M book accretion above the full-year forecast; the 20% liquidity discount is unsourced (ADTV is Rp159.1m/day, 0.009% of market cap, so the size is right but the only sentence on it says IDR159,072,601.6bn a day, a 1,000x unit error that reads as the opposite); COE sits under the card's band floor of 7.45+5.0 = 12.45%. Removing the 20% discount still gives 36 vs 90, so the stack does not by itself move the rating.

calibration.note: Gate passes at -0.32pp but only because both sides come from S0-era figures; FY+1 ROE 1.567% is 17% below the FY2025 actual 1.883% with no drift justification, and FY2026E profit is cut 15% while 9M2026 equity rose Rp118.7bn. The BLOCK drift.cti justification also misdescribes the model ('flat nominal cost base' while opex rises 1,134 to 1,395, +4.2% a year).

signoff.notes: Call supported, verified line by line. Blend 0.45x41.6 + 0.55x7.8 = 23.0 (engine v0 22.9995); x1.1185 = 25.7 base; 0.5x25.7 + 0.25x20.9 + 0.25x61.2 = 33.4; x0.8 liquidity = 26.7 -> 27. Decisive test: the SELL survives removal of its most contestable piece. On the warranted multiple alone (0.1218x BVPS 341.3 = Rp41.6, from (3.2%-2.0%)/(11.85%-2.0%)) the target would be Rp37, still -59% to the Rp90 price; only the 55% residual-income weight takes it to 27, so no part of the rating depends on the C3 terminal-value dispute. The dilution arithmetic checks: par conversion Rp3.0tn/Rp100 = 30.0bn shares; probability-weighted 0.7x30.0 + 0.2x33.3 (market 90) + 0.1x8.85 (book 339) = 28.55bn, total 48.50bn; at v0 the transfer is 23.0x(1 - 19.953/48.55) = Rp13.54 = Rp270.1bn, matching the bridge. Ordinal check that the bridge is not double-counted: the two consistent treatments - advance stripped from book (0.1218 x 188 = Rp22.9, undiluted) and full book with pro-rata dilution (27 x 19.953/48.55 = Rp11.1) - bracket the Rp27 pre-conversion target. No conservatism stack: sustainable ROE 3.2% is above FY2025A 1.92%, FY2024A 2.75% and the model FY2030E 3.0% (F32); CTI 84->78% and NIM 2.19->3.3% both favour the company; credit cost 0.50% is below, not above, the system ~2%. CET1 36.02% x RWA 18,415 = Rp6,634bn, above the Rp6tn KBMI II line, so the return-of-advance argument holds. Batch bias: BANKS is two-sided (BBYB/NOBU/BBRI BUY v BNBA/BBHI/BBMD/BGTG SELL, MCOR REDUCE), so no shared-cause tilt; BACA is idiosyncratic to the unconverted advance and consistent with the INDO rate-sensitive AVOID stance. All five FIXes are non-material to the call, and each correction points towards a weaker company, so none of them is propping up the SELL: Q1 means audited PPOP is Rp186.7bn, not 206.0; Q4 means holding CTI at 84.6% is worth less than the drift; Q3 moves the disclosed post-conversion value from 13.5 to 11.1. None touches rating, target, weights or a first-year input. Note for v2, mandatory text fixes: (Q2, fix before publication if any single item is fixed) F23 is correctly 79.0bn shares but the money filter prefixes IDR and s5 renders 79m - the summary must read 79.0bn authorised against 19,953m issued and 59,047m unissued, and s5 "authorised capital of 79.0bn shares accommodates any of our cases"; the present text makes the central dilution case read as impossible. (Q1) s3 and the summary must stop citing the pack lines 578.8/649.0/1,227.8/206.0 to S2: preferred fix is to restate nii/noii from F7/F10 for FY2025A and FY2024A (the engine already restates opex, pbt, equity and shares this way, and FY2026E moves by under Rp1bn of PPOP, so there is no valuation consequence), and to state the audited 84.6% CTI; fallback is to label them engine-basis, drop [S2] and remove the s3 line-81 claim to quote F7/F10. As printed the FY2025A column is arithmetically impossible: PPOP 206.0 less provisions 4.174 and non-operating 19.271 cannot reach the restated PBT 163.3. (Q4) rewrite drift.cti to the actual mechanism - TOI +32% (NII 752.9->1,116.2 on 9% loan growth) against opex +23% (1,134.0->1,394.8), i.e. about 1.2pp of CTI a year from operating leverage, not a flat nominal cost base - and delete the unimplemented insurance-premium netting, which cannot occur under opex = toi x cti. (Q3) state the post-conversion value on the target basis (Rp11.1 = 27 x 19.953/48.55; target-level bridge Rp317bn / Rp15.9 per share) and label 13.5, if kept, as the v0-basis figure. (Q5) replace "CASA is thin / no split by product" with S2 p.108 (giro 2,593.7 / tabungan 4,365.0 / deposito 11,295.3 = 38.1% CASA FY2025, 43.3% Sep-2026 per S4) and re-argue the deposit beta off that mix; s1 already says the base is transactional and contradicts s2. (Q6) one free-float figure, 25.30% public from S2 p.88. (Q7) print 5.75% (F39), not 5.8% - the pctv filter still rounds it despite the accepted C11 correction.

bias.note: Base FY2026E net profit falls 15% to Rp106.7bn on the credit charge normalising from 0.04% to 0.50% and CTI held at 84%, while terminal ROE 3.2% is above FY2025A's 1.9% [S2]; the -20% deposit path is sourced to the Sep-2026 monthly (TPF Rp14,272bn vs Rp18,254bn at FY2025) [S4]; bear and bull mirror the same four shocks (credit 1.0%/0.2%, NIM -/+0.4pp, loans -/+4pp, CTI +/-4pp) at 50/25/25. No unsourced conservatism or optimism moves the rating: the SELL rests on the unconverted Rp3.0tn advance, the diluted book and RI below COE.

recomputed.item: FY2025A pre-provision operating profit (NII 553.598 + NOII 654.887 - opex 1,021.784)

findings.finding: s3 and the summary quote the data pack's FY2025 lines as audited S2: NII Rp578.8bn (F7 Rp553.6bn), NOII Rp649.0bn (F10 Rp654.9bn), TOI Rp1,227.8bn (audited Rp1,208.5bn) and PPOP Rp206.0bn (audited Rp186.7bn, 10% higher), while s3 line 81 states the report quotes F7/F10. The bank template's pack:nii cannot be restated, so the engine line must be labelled as such, not cited to S2.

F23 is recorded as 79.0bn, so the money/num0 filters render the summary as 'IDR79.0bn of authorised but unissued shares' and s5 as 'authorised capital of 79m shares accommodates any of our cases'. The LK shows 79,000,000,000 shares authorised, 19,953,024,885 issued and 59,047m unissued (S2 p.373), so the ~30,000m-share par conversion is well inside the articles; the text understates the headroom by 1000x and makes the central dilution case look impossible as printed.

The disclosed post-conversion value of ~Rp13.5 subtracts a bridge struck at v0 (Rp23.0/share: 23.0 x 19.953/48.55 = Rp9.46 post, gap Rp13.54 x 19.953m = Rp270.1bn) from the Rp27 target. At the target level the post-conversion value is 27 x 19.953/48.55 = Rp11.1, so the disclosed figure is ~22% too high and is not on the same value basis as the bridge.

The drift.cti justification says CTI falls from 84% to 78% 'on a flat nominal cost base', but model opex rises Rp1,134.0bn to Rp1,394.8bn (+23%) over FY2026-30E, and the stated mechanism (the Rp581.4bn insurance premium stopping) is not implemented: opex is set as toi x cti, so the premium never leaves the cost base.

s2 states 'CASA is thin' and 'the bank does not disclose the split by product', but S2 p.108 discloses giro Rp2,593.7bn (14.2%), tabungan Rp4,365.0bn (23.9%) and deposito Rp11,295.3bn (61.9%) at FY2025 - CASA 38.1% - and S4 shows CASA 43.3% at 30 Sep 2026.
